scene: two full adults, both drawn head to feet. On the left a man in a cap walks to the right carrying a closed cardboard box level in both hands. On the right a woman stands in an open doorway of her own plain house, the open door swung back beside her, both hands held out open at waist height to receive the box, smiling and looking at the box. A clear gap of floor lies between the box and her hands: the box is still in the carrier's hands and has not been handed over yet. Above the head of the CARRIER (the man in the cap) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a person carrying a box towards a second person who waits at an open door with open hands.
avoid: a hand or arm coming out of a door with no person attached (nobody may be cut off by the door frame); the box already in the second person's hands (geven); a box put down on a doorstep with nobody there (zetten); a crate on the head (dragen); a van at the kerb (rijden).
alt: Een man loopt met een doos naar een vrouw die met open handen in een open deur staat te wachten.
example_nl: Ik breng de kinderen naar school.
example_en: I take the children to school.

scene: one adult walks from left to right over empty ground, caught mid-stride: the front foot flat on the ground, the back foot just lifted on its toes, the arms swinging in opposition, back straight, eyes ahead. Nothing else in the picture.
must: an ordinary unhurried walk, one foot down and one just leaving the ground.
avoid: both feet off the ground and the body leaning forward (rennen); a raised knee and a straight swinging arm (marcheren); a person standing still beside a bicycle (fietsen); a walking stick; speed lines or dust puffs.
alt: Een volwassene is midden in een stap: de voorste voet staat plat op de grond, de achterste voet is net van de vloer.
example_nl: Ik loop naar de supermarkt.
example_en: I walk to the supermarket.

scene: two full adults, both drawn head to feet, at a garden gate. A plain fence of three bold rails runs across the picture with a fixed post at each side; the gate leaf is swung wide open on its hinges and the gap is clearly empty. On the left the host stands beside the open gate, smiling, one arm stretched out with an open palm sweeping towards the gap in a clear 'go ahead' gesture, the other thumb raised. On the right the visitor is mid-step walking through the gap, looking at the host and smiling. No barrier arm, no pole, no sign. Above the head of the HOST (the person giving permission) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: one person with an open welcoming hand and a thumb up, letting a second person walk through an open gate.
avoid: any long pole or barrier arm above a head (it reads as a floating plank); a flat palm held up to stop someone (stoppen); a heavy sack (moeten); a flexed fist (kunnen); coins or a ticket (betalen); a sign or arrow.
alt: Een man staat naast een open hek en wuift een vrouw die erdoor loopt met open hand en duim omhoog welkom.
example_nl: Je mag hier niet parkeren.
example_en: You are not allowed to park here.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with a closed notebook and a closed pen case in front of them; the hands lift the front cover, raised a hand width off the table, the first blank page showing. The moment is the cover coming up, not later.
must: the cover of a closed notebook being lifted for the first time.
avoid: an open notebook already half full on the table (schrijven); a hand placed flat on a shut book with the pen lid on (wachten); a person walking through an open door into a room (verlaten); a bell or a whistle; a stopwatch.
alt: Een volwassene zit aan een tafel en tilt net het voorplat van een gesloten schrift op, met een dichte pennenbak ernaast.
example_nl: De les begint om negen uur.
example_en: The lesson begins at nine o'clock.

scene: one adult kneels on one knee on the floor in the middle of a plain room, bent forward and looking hard at the floor, holding a large round magnifying glass in one hand out in front of them and close to the ground, with the other hand pressed on the floor for balance. A low sofa stands behind them. Nothing of the lost object is visible and nothing is being opened or lifted.
must: a person on one knee peering through a magnifying glass held low over the floor, hunting for something.
avoid: a cushion lifted on the knee or a box being opened (it reads as unwrapping); an object held up in a raised hand (vinden); keys left on a table (vergeten); an eye to a microscope on a table (onderzoeken); a hand shielding the eyes looking into the distance (kijken).
alt: Een volwassene knielt in een kamer en speurt met een vergrootglas vlak boven de vloer.
example_nl: Ik zoek mijn telefoon.
example_en: I am looking for my phone.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with an open book lying flat in front of them, both hands resting at its edges, the head bowed and the eyes on the pages; the pages show short plain lines of print and no letters. A mug stands off to the side, untouched.
must: eyes turned down on an open book held flat on the table.
avoid: a pen touching the paper (schrijven); a laptop screen with both hands on the keys (werken); a person holding a book up with one finger marking the place (leren); a closed book.
alt: Een volwassene zit aan een tafel met een open boek, beide handen aan de rand en de ogen op de bladzijden.
example_nl: Hij leest een boek in bed.
example_en: He reads a book in bed.

scene: one adult lies flat on their back on a made bed on top of the covers, both arms at their sides, the head on a pillow, eyes wide open and looking up at the ceiling. The blanket is not pulled up and the knees are straight. Nothing else in the room.
must: a person flat on their back on the bed with both eyes open.
avoid: closed eyes and a blanket pulled up to the chin (slapen); the body bent up at the waist with the feet on the floor (zitten); the body curled on one side with both knees drawn up (slapen); a book or a phone in the hands.
alt: Een volwassene rust met gestrekte benen op de rug op een opgemaakt bed, de ogen open en naar boven gericht.
example_nl: Het boek ligt op de grond.
example_en: The book is lying on the floor.

scene: two full adults facing each other across a plain shop counter, both drawn head to feet. On the left the BUYER stands in front of the counter with a small shopping basket on one arm and holds a folded banknote out towards the seller. On the right the SELLER stands behind the counter in a plain apron with a large chunky cash register on the counter at the seller's side and a paper bag of apples on the counter, not yet picked up. The note is still in the buyer's hand. Above the head of the BUYER (the left person) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who is performing the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: the buyer, marked by the arrow, holding out money to a seller who has a cash register.
avoid: an arrow over the seller; the bag already in the buyer's hand (finished sale); a close-up price tag or till display (betalen); a bag carried away with a coin still in the hand (halen); the seller holding out the bag with the customer's hands empty (verkopen); a credit card; any text or numbers on the register.
alt: Een klant, aangewezen met een pijl, houdt een briefje geld naar een verkoper achter een toonbank met een kassa.
example_nl: Ik wil een nieuwe fiets kopen.
example_en: I want to buy a new bike.

scene: one adult walks away from a small table, looking back over one shoulder with a slight frown; a bunch of keys on a round ring lies alone on the table behind them, and one hand is raised to the side of the head.
must: keys left behind on the table while the person walks off.
avoid: a person kneeling to look under a sofa (zoeken); the keys held up in triumph (vinden); a crossed-out calendar; a hand over the mouth.
alt: Iemand loopt bij een tafel vandaan en kijkt om; op de tafel blijft een bos sleutels liggen.
example_nl: Ik ben mijn paraplu vergeten.
example_en: I have forgotten my umbrella.

scene: one adult is caught off balance on empty ground: the body tilted sharply forward with both arms flung out, the back foot off the ground, the front heel just lifting, the mouth open and the eyes wide. Neither hand touches the floor and the body is still above it.
must: an adult tipping over in mid-air with both arms flung out.
avoid: both feet flat with the body bent at the waist and the hands on the knees (bukken); a person already on the floor with one hand pushing the ground (opstaan); a person crouching on a low stool (zitten); a pushed-over chair.
alt: Een volwassene raakt uit balans: het lichaam helt voorover, beide armen zwaaien en de achterste voet is los van de grond.
example_nl: De appel valt van de boom.
example_en: The apple falls from the tree.

scene: one adult sits behind the steering wheel of a plain car seen from the side, both hands on the wheel and eyes on the road ahead; the headlights are lit and the wheels sit on a stretch of road with a single white dashed line. Through the window only the driver is visible.
must: a person at a steering wheel with the car on a road.
avoid: a bare bicycle with a rider leaning forward (fietsen); a person standing beside an open bonnet (repareren); a hand on a bus door handle (instappen); a person walking along the road (lopen); an aeroplane above clouds (vliegen).
alt: Een volwassene zit achter het stuur van een auto op een weg met een witte streep, de handen aan het wiel.
example_nl: Mijn vader rijdt een rode auto.
example_en: My father drives a red car.

scene: one adult stands at a plain table with two jars side by side, one tall and one round; the right hand is lifted and held still open above the round jar, both eyes on it. The hand has not touched a jar.
must: one hand hovering above one of two jars while the other jar stays untouched.
avoid: two jars already in the hands and both carried (dragen); one jar lifted off the table and held up (nemen); coins counted into a palm (betalen); a person pointing with a straight finger at a menu (wijzen).
alt: Een volwassene staat bij een tafel met twee potten en houdt de hand boven een van de twee, zonder die aan te raken.
example_nl: Ik moet een toetje kiezen.
example_en: I have to choose a dessert.

scene: one adult sits at a table with a single sheet of paper flat in front of them, a pen gripped in one hand with the nib pressed to the paper, a short line of plain marks just made, and the eyes on the tip. The other hand holds the paper steady.
must: a pen point pressed to paper on which marks have just appeared.
avoid: eyes on grey print lines inside an open book (lezen); a keyboard under both hands (werken); a brush with a picture on the page (tekenen); a pen held up and capped.
alt: Een volwassene zit aan een tafel en duwt een pen op een vel papier waarop al een paar korte strepen staan.
example_nl: Ik schrijf een brief aan mijn tante.
example_en: I write a letter to my aunt.

scene: one adult lies in a bed with the blanket pulled up to the shoulders, the head on a pillow, both eyes closed, the mouth relaxed and both arms outside the covers. The room is dim and a round alarm clock sits on a small bedside table.
must: closed eyes and the face at rest under the blanket.
avoid: open eyes looking at the ceiling with the blanket flat (liggen); a person sitting up on the floor with the head on a table (zitten); wide open mouth and a hand over it (geeuwen); a person walking in pyjamas (lopen).
alt: Een volwassene ligt onder een deken tot de schouders, de ogen dicht en het gezicht rustig; naast het bed staat een wekker.
example_nl: De baby slaapt in de kamer.
example_en: The baby sleeps in the room.

scene: one adult stands facing the viewer with one hand raised to chest height, the palm turned up and the fingers spread, mouth open mid-word; the other hand rests at the side. A single bold speech bubble with a plain line inside floats beside the head, and no second person is in the picture.
must: one adult mid-word with a speech bubble, facing the viewer alone.
avoid: a second person facing them, both with short bars in two bubbles (praten); two bubbles and one hand passing a box (vertellen); a phone at the ear (bellen); a row of listeners in chairs (luisteren); letters inside the bubble.
alt: Een volwassene staat alleen voor de kijker met een open hand op borsthoogte en de mond open; naast het hoofd hangt een tekstballon.
example_nl: Zij spreekt goed Nederlands.
example_en: She speaks good Dutch.

scene: one adult walks left to right carrying a tall cardboard box with both arms wrapped around it, the box pressed against the chest and high enough to hide the chin, the back leaning slightly away from the weight, the eyes peering over the top edge of the box.
must: both arms hugging a tall box against the chest while walking.
avoid: a crate balanced on the head with both arms up (brengen); a box passing from hand to hand between two people (geven); an arm hanging down with a shopping bag in the fingers (houden); a person lifting a box off the floor (tillen).
alt: Een volwassene loopt met een hoge doos tegen de borst, de armen eromheen en de kin erachter verborgen.
example_nl: Zij draagt een zware doos naar boven.
example_en: She carries a heavy box upstairs.

scene: one adult stands on a low step with both arms raised in a V and an open mouth, a cup held high in one hand; a small rosette is pinned to the chest and pieces of paper fall around them. One other adult stands behind, looking down, arms hanging, holding nothing.
must: one adult with both arms up and a cup held high, a paper rosette on the chest.
avoid: one adult alone holding up a key with a quiet smile (vinden); two people shaking hands at a table with coins on it (delen); a person running past a ribbon (rennen); a crowd and a stadium; a scoreboard with figures.
alt: Een volwassene steekt beide armen omhoog met een beker in een hand, een rozet op de borst en papieren snippers in de lucht.
example_nl: Ons team wint de wedstrijd.
example_en: Our team wins the match.

scene: one adult sits relaxed on a plain chair with the head tipped back, both eyes closed and a wide open smile; one hand holds a full steaming cup close under the nose, and nothing else is in the room.
must: a wide closed-eyed smile with a cup held under the nose.
avoid: an open mouth with both hands on the belly and the head thrown back (lachen); a person holding up a cup as a prize (winnen); a fork lifted to an open mouth (eten); a nose bent close to food on a table (ruiken); a sun or a heart drawn above the head.
alt: Een volwassene zit met het hoofd achterover en de ogen dicht te glimlachen, een volle kop onder de neus.
example_nl: Wij genieten van het mooie weer.
example_en: We enjoy the lovely weather.

scene: SKIP: a beginning out of nothing has no single picturable action; a flame, a chick from an egg or a sprouting seed each read as a literal object (branden, uitkomen, groeien) rather than as this verb.

one adult stands braced with both feet apart and leans back, both hands closed around a long rope that runs over the shoulder towards the right edge of the frame; the elbows bend, the rope is taut, and nothing is attached at the far end.
must: a taut rope taken in both hands with the body leaning back.
avoid: a rope slack in one hand with both people close together (houden); a palm flat against a box and pushing it forward (duwen); a heavy box wrapped in both arms (dragen); a horse or a cart at the end of the rope; a winch.
alt: Een volwassene staat schrap met beide voeten uit elkaar en houdt een strak touw met twee handen vast, het lichaam achterover.
example_nl: Ik trek aan het touw.
example_en: I pull on the rope.

scene: SKIP: understanding has no single picturable action; the lightbulb bubble belongs to weten on the A0 page and the same head-and-bubble picture would turn into that card.

one adult at a plain counter holds out one folded banknote flat on an open palm towards a shopkeeper, who stands facing them with a lamp in one hand and the other palm raised and turned down. The note is offered and not yet taken, and no till or price card is in the frame. Above the head of the CUSTOMER offering the note floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a note held out flat on an open palm towards a shopkeeper who has not taken it.
avoid: a note pushed flat along the counter beside a paper bag (kopen); one hand held palm-up and empty with no note (vragen); a cardboard box passing between two people (geven); a note pressed back into the same hand (krijgen).
alt: Een volwassene houdt een opgevouwen briefje op een open handpalm naar de winkelier, die een lamp vasthoudt en de andere hand ophoudt.
example_nl: Zij bieden ons thee.
example_en: They offer us tea.

scene: one adult steps through a plain doorway out of a room, seen from behind, one foot already on the far side of the threshold; the near hand pulls the door shut behind them, so the room with one chair inside is only half visible. The direction of travel is out, away from the chair.
must: a person seen from behind stepping out through a door and pulling it shut.
avoid: both people facing each other across a threshold with two open palms (praten); a person standing still inside a room beside a chair (blijven); a hand laid on a door handle with the body facing the room (sluiten); a person arriving through the door towards the viewer (komen).
alt: Een volwassene stapt met de rug naar ons door een deuropening naar buiten en trekt de deur achter zich dicht.
example_nl: Wij verlaten het gebouw om vijf uur.
example_en: We leave the building at five o'clock.

scene: one adult stands with the head tipped back and a plain glass held to the lips with one hand, the glass tilted and half empty, a few drops at the rim, the eyes shut. The other hand hangs at the side. A full jug of water stands on a table to the side.
must: a tilted glass at the lips with the head tipped back.
avoid: a plate, a fork and a full mouth (eten); a raised bottle held away from the mouth (proosten); a closed cup on a table with both hands beside it (wachten); a tap running into a sink (wassen).
alt: Een volwassene staat met het hoofd achterover en een schuin gehouden halfleeg glas aan de lippen; naast hem staat een kan water.
example_nl: Ik drink elke ochtend thee.
example_en: I drink tea every morning.

scene: SKIP: seeming is a judgement, not an action; the only honest pictogram is a comparison of two identical portraits, which is a sign rather than one moment of an action.

one adult faces a door from inside the room and pushes it shut with the flat of one hand on the door face, the other hand on the handle; the door is a hand width from its frame, with a dark sliver of the room beyond still showing and the person looking at the gap.
must: a door pushed nearly shut with a hand flat on it and a sliver of gap left.
avoid: a person seen from behind stepping out through a doorway (verlaten); a key turned in a lock with a padlock visible (op slot doen); a hand held flat high on a barrier beside a round sign (mogen); a wide-open door with the frame empty.
alt: Een volwassene duwt van binnen met een vlakke hand een deur dicht, met nog een smalle kier en het oog op die kier.
example_nl: De winkel sluit om zes uur.
example_en: The shop closes at six o'clock.

scene: two full adults facing each other across a plain shop counter, both drawn head to feet. On the right the SELLER stands behind the counter in a plain apron with a large chunky cash register on the counter at the seller's side, and holds out a paper bag of apples with both hands across the counter towards the customer. On the left the CUSTOMER stands in front of the counter with a small shopping basket on one arm and the other hand at the side, empty. No banknote is in any hand. Above the head of the SELLER (the right person) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who is performing the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: the seller, marked by the arrow, holding out a bag of apples across a counter to a customer; the cash register beside them.
avoid: an arrow over the customer; the customer holding out a note (kopen); the bag already in the customer's hands; a note pushed across the counter (betalen); an empty stall with no person behind it (huren); two adults shaking hands (delen).
alt: Een verkoper, aangewezen met een pijl, houdt een zak appels over de toonbank naar een klant; naast de verkoper staat een kassa.
example_nl: Hij wil zijn oude auto verkopen.
example_en: He wants to sell his old car.

scene: one adult stands side-on and swings a flat wooden bat down onto a ball in the air at hip height; both hands grip the handle, the elbows bent, the shoulders turned and the eyes on the ball. The ball has just left the bat and the ground below is empty.
must: a flat bat swung with both hands at a small ball in the air.
avoid: a hand flat on a door pushing it shut (sluiten); two open palms meeting high above the head (klappen); a hammer on a nail in a plank (hameren); a fist drawn back with nothing in front of it (meppen).
alt: Een volwassene staat opzij en zwaait een houten slagplank met beide handen naar een balletje in de lucht.
example_nl: Je mag een kind niet slaan.
example_en: You must not hit a child.

scene: one adult kneels beside a bicycle and lifts a flat tyre out of the front fork with both hands, a small pump and a second tyre already on the ground beside them; the old tyre is clear of the rim and held up, and the rest of the bicycle stays whole.
must: a flat tyre held up in both hands, clear of the bicycle wheel.
avoid: a pump in one hand against a bare tyre (repareren); a box carried towards a half-open door (brengen); one note offered flat on a palm (bieden); a coin and a price sign on a counter (betalen).
alt: Iemand houdt op de hurken bij een fiets een lekke band omhoog, los van het wiel.
example_nl: Ik moet de lamp vervangen.
example_en: I have to replace the lamp.

scene: one adult stands in front of a picture hanging on a wall and leans in with both hands behind the back and the eyes fixed on the frame; the picture shows two plain shapes. A second adult is not in the room, and no other object is in the frame.
must: one adult leaning towards a hanging framed picture, hands behind the back.
avoid: two people facing each other with a bar above each head (praten); a leaflet held in two hands before the eyes (lezen); a hand behind an ear beside a radio (luisteren); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken).
alt: Iemand staat voor een ingelijste tekening en kijkt er voorover naar.
example_nl: Wij bekijken samen de huizen.
example_en: We look at the houses together.

scene: one adult stands at a plain table with the shoulders slumped and the head low, both hands in the pockets, looking down at a small chessboard on the table where only black pieces stand; a folded paper rosette torn in two lies next to the board, and no other person is in the picture.
must: a slumped figure looking down at a chessboard with nothing of theirs left on it.
avoid: one adult with both arms raised and a cup held high (winnen); a hand closing over a key on the ground (vinden); a person on their knees reaching under a sofa (zoeken); a purse with coins spilled on the floor (vallen).
alt: Een volwassene staat met hangende schouders bij een schaakbord met alleen zwarte stukken en een gescheurd rozet ernaast.
example_nl: Hij verliest altijd zijn sleutels.
example_en: He always loses his keys.

scene: SKIP: providing is giving plus a need, and the giving half would be the picture of geven or brengen on another page; nothing on the frame marks out who is being provided for.

one adult stands at a plain table bent forward with one eye to the eyepiece of a bold simple microscope that stands on the table, one hand on the microscope's focus knob; a small open notebook and a pencil lie on the table beside it. No magnifying glass, no bicycle, no second person.
must: a person with an eye to a microscope on a table, a notebook beside it.
avoid: a hand-held magnifying glass (zoeken); a person kneeling on the floor (zoeken); a person leaning at a hanging picture (bekijken); a hammer and planks (maken); a pointer on a wall chart (wijzen).
alt: Iemand buigt zich aan een tafel over een microscoop, met een schrift ernaast.
example_nl: De politie gaat de zaak onderzoeken.
example_en: The police are going to investigate the case.

scene: two adults stand in a doorway facing each other: the visitor steps in with a bunch of flowers held out in both hands, and the resident stands back with a hand on the open door and smiles. Behind the resident a lit room is visible, and the doorway frames both. Above the head of the VISITOR with the flowers floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a bunch of flowers held out in a doorway to a person who has the door open.
avoid: a box carried away towards a closed door and laid down outside (brengen); one adult walking alone through an empty room (wonen); two adults at a market stall (kopen); a crowd of many people in a hall.
alt: Iemand stapt in de deuropening binnen met een bos bloemen voor een ander.
example_nl: Ik bezoek mijn opa in het ziekenhuis.
example_en: I visit my grandfather in the hospital.

scene: one adult stands facing slightly away with the head thrown back, the mouth wide open, both eyes squeezed shut in curved lines, one hand flat on the belly and the shoulders lifted; the chest is clearly shaking. The mouth is open for laughing, with no sound shown.
must: a head thrown back with a wide open mouth and eyes squeezed shut.
avoid: a person alone with a hand raised and a speech bubble, the mouth open in words (spreken); a person with the head tipped back beside an open notebook (zingen); a hand over the mouth with wide eyes (schrikken); a single tear on a straight face (huilen); a smiling face with the mouth closed.
alt: Een volwassene gooit het hoofd achterover met een wijd open mond, de ogen tot streepjes dicht en een hand op de buik.
example_nl: Wij lachen om de grap.
example_en: We laugh at the joke.

scene: one adult stands in the middle of empty ground with the head slightly lifted and the mouth open, one hand pressed flat on the chest, the other stretched out to the side, eyes closed. A few bold curved lines spread from the open mouth, and no other person or object is in the picture.
must: an open mouth with curved lines spreading from it, one hand on the chest.
avoid: a face bent double with a hand on the belly (lachen); a microphone at the mouth (spreken); a tall stand with a sheet of paper on it (lezen); a guitar or a piano; letters inside the curved lines.
alt: Een volwassene staat alleen met het hoofd iets geheven en de mond open; uit de mond waaieren een paar gebogen lijnen.
example_nl: Zij zingt een mooi lied.
example_en: She sings a beautiful song.

scene: a small aeroplane in side view travels level across an empty sky, wings straight and nose slightly up, with two bold flat clouds below it and no ground in the picture; a pilot's head shows in the cockpit window.
must: an aeroplane in the air with clouds below it.
avoid: a bird with both wings spread (fladderen); an aeroplane touching a runway (landen); a hot-air balloon leaving a field (stijgen); a person with both arms out jumping (springen); a jet trail across the sky.
alt: Een klein toestel met vleugels gaat horizontaal door de lucht, boven twee platte wolken.
example_nl: De vogel vliegt over het huis.
example_en: The bird flies over the house.

scene: One adult stands facing the viewer in a plain room, drawn head to feet. Both arms hang free at the sides with the hands open and empty. The body is inside a long buttoned coat, closed across the chest, the sleeves reaching the wrists, the collar up at the neck. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a buttoned coat worn on the body, both hands empty at the sides.
avoid: both arms hugging a tall box against the chest (dragen); a jumper pulled down over a raised head (aantrekken); a folded coat carried over one forearm (houden); a coat on a hook beside a person in underclothes (uittrekken).
alt: Een volwassene staat rechtop met lege, open handen naast het lichaam en een dichte jas met knopen aan.
example_nl: Zij draagt vandaag een rode jas.
example_en: She is wearing a red coat today.

scene: A large round sun with straight rays sits in a clear sky above a grass lawn with one bench. There is no person in this picture, only the sun, its rays falling on the lawn and bench, and a few short shadows. No text, no clouds, no numbers.
must: a bright round sun with rays falling on a lawn.
avoid: a person holding a torch beam on a wall (schijnen); a sun hidden behind rain clouds (regenen); a person sweating with a fan (zweten); a sun low over the sea at dusk (ondergaan); a thermometer.
alt: Een grote ronde zon met rechte stralen staat boven een grasveld met een bank; er is niemand te zien.
example_nl: Vandaag schijnt de zon de hele dag.
example_en: Today the sun shines all day.

scene: One adult stands in a street patting both empty coat pockets with wide eyes and an open mouth, alarmed. A little way behind them on the pavement a bunch of keys on a ring lies unnoticed. The adult is not looking at the keys.
must: empty pockets patted while keys lie unseen behind.
avoid: two people at a chessboard, one tipping over a king (verliezen); keys left on a table while walking away (vergeten); a person kneeling to look under a sofa (zoeken); keys held up in triumph (vinden); a hand over the mouth.
alt: Een volwassene klopt in paniek op lege jaszakken terwijl achter hen op straat een bos sleutels ligt.
example_nl: Ik ben mijn sleutels weer kwijt, ik verlies alles.
example_en: I have lost my keys again, I lose everything.
